inputs.resume_text:
Ritika Banerjee
PGDHRM 2025-27 | Indian Institute of Management Ranchi | ritika.b@iimranchi.ac.in

EDUCATION
PGDHRM, IIM Ranchi, 2025-27, CGPA 7.8/10
BA (Hons) Psychology, Lady Shri Ram College, Delhi University, 2025, 8.6/10

SUMMER INTERNSHIP
Mahindra & Mahindra, Automotive Sector, Nashik plant | HR Intern | Apr - Jun 2026
- Analysed exit interviews of 380 shop-floor associates; found 58% of first-year exits cited shift allocation, and proposed a shift-preference window that the plant HR head approved for 2 lines
- Designed a 5-day onboarding buddy program for diploma trainees; first cohort of 46 trainees rated it 4.4/5
- Redesigned the grievance tracker in Excel so the IR team could see open cases by line and age

INTERNSHIPS
Teach For India | Fellowship Recruitment Intern | Dec 2024 - Feb 2025
- Screened 600 applications and conducted 40 first-round phone interviews

POSITIONS OF RESPONSIBILITY
- Placement Committee member, IIM Ranchi (2025-26): coordinate with 18 recruiters for HR and general management roles
- President, Psychology Society, LSR (2024-25): ran a mental health awareness week with 1,200 attendees

ACHIEVEMENTS
- National winner, Tata Steel HR case competition "HRchitect" 2026

plan.warmup_question: What has kept you busy in the last few weeks at IIM Ranchi?
plan.background_question: Walk me through your path from psychology at LSR to your PGDHRM and the experiences that shaped your interest in HR.

slots.core_question: I see you analysed exit interviews at Mahindra & Mahindra’s Nashik plant. What did you do to turn that analysis into a shift-preference proposal?
slots.intent_private: Needs Ritika’s specific analytical steps, her personal decisions, how the 58% finding was established, why the proposal was chosen, and what she took from the internship or would do differently now.
likely_probes: Which part of the analysis was yours?
What evidence led you to recommend a preference window?
What would you do differently now?

slots.core_question: I see you coordinated with 18 recruiters on IIM Ranchi’s placement committee. What was the hardest coordination challenge you handled?
slots.intent_private: Needs a specific recruiter-coordination situation, Ritika’s actions and judgment, how she managed competing expectations, and the outcome for the placement process.
likely_probes: What part of that challenge did you personally own?
How did you decide what to communicate first?
What changed as a result of your intervention?

slots.core_question: How would you handle a shop-floor employee who believes their shift allocation was unfair?
slots.intent_private: Needs an applied employee-relations response covering fact-finding, procedural fairness, confidentiality, consistency with policy, escalation, and communicating closure without prejudging the grievance.
likely_probes: Why would you begin with that approach?
When might that approach not be appropriate?
How have you handled a similar concern in your own work?

slots.core_question: After your psychology degree and HR summer internship, what is drawing you to build your career in human resources?
slots.intent_private: Needs a reason grounded in Ritika’s psychology background and Mahindra experience, plus a specific aspect of an HR role she wants to pursue rather than a generic interest in people or business.
likely_probes: Which part of your Mahindra experience most shaped that choice?
What HR responsibility would you want to take on early in your career?

plan.plan_notes: The plan prioritizes the strongest and most relevant summer-internship claim, then tests stakeholder coordination through the placement committee. A practical employee-relations question adds depth beyond the resume’s quantified achievements, while the final motivation question explores her path from psychology through HR internships into a long-term HR career.
